svg.title: Layout of the census metadata block
svg.desc: The census metadata block of the 2.0 coder stream to scale, with the head with the forms of the eight kinds of place, a run with one byte per page, and the records sorted by kind; one real record as byte boxes with the fed bytes, the estimates of some of its values, a list flag of a second record, and how the decoder restores the page.
svg.text: Layout of the census metadata block
9,280,775 B of the coder stream behind the metadata block, one record for each of 36,148 census pages that follow the template form
head with the forms 5,438 B and the run 55,931 B, then the records 9.22 MB, by kind of place, each kind in page order

text.tspan: per kind its positions, per position its variants, per variant its value fields
one byte per page from the first to the last page with a record, the kind of place of its record or none

svg.text: fed to the models, not coded
... one flag for each of the 57 positions
48 values in the order of the number coder. All gap bits of this record are predicted; 8 of them mark kept text in the stub.

text.tspan: estimate from the values coded before, true value, token

svg.text: Estimates. A rule gives some values exactly (empty token). The other numbers are estimated by an online ridge regression
per kind of place and field over values of the same record and the mean of the field over the 8 nearest earlier places
of that kind, with an offset per state.
County. Its rank in a list of the county records of the state is coded. The name fills the value slot of the intro
sentence, and the category line repeats it without a value. Name and state of the place are placeholders.

text.tspan: record of Kennett, Missouri, page 200,398, 169 B at 5,887,733

svg.text: two units of the interwiki position; the names stay in the stub

text.tspan: restores each census page from four parts

svg.text: Fed to the models, not coded. In front of the flags the revision id and the day of the page from the metadata block (coarse),
in front of each flag its position, in front of each value its field and a scale class of the estimate, and in front
of a value without a field the earlier value of the record that it most likely repeats.
